prohibited_recommendations: Do not reassure a patient with a normal screening score when instrumental and occupational function have been lost
Do not accept the patient's own minimising account as the functional history when insight is reduced
Do not allow continued unsupervised professional practice with fiduciary responsibility and a 1st-percentile planning score
Do not leave driving unaddressed after two reported near-misses with a documented dysexecutive syndrome
Do not add aspirin to clopidogrel: long-term dual antiplatelet therapy has no indication four years after a lacunar stroke and raises bleeding risk
required_recommendations: Diagnose major vascular cognitive disorder of subcortical small-vessel type despite the MoCA of 26/30: occupational and instrumental independence are lost (FAQ 23/30) [VASCOG_2014]
Advise him to stop driving now, pending a formal driving assessment, because of the two near-misses, and explain the duty to inform the licensing authority

Advise that he stop independent professional practice, with his consent involve his business partner or occupational health, and start legal and financial planning (lasting power of attorney) while he can take part
Lower blood pressure gradually to below 130/80 mmHg (148/88 today), checking orthostatic BP at each change [AHA_ASA_2021_secondary]
Intensify the statin to atorvastatin 80 mg (LDL 108 mg/dL on 40 mg) and continue single antiplatelet therapy with clopidogrel after the lacunar stroke [AHA_ASA_2021_secondary]
Keep the HbA1c target individualised at about below 8.0% (7.9% now) and avoid adding agents that cause hypoglycaemia; advise reducing alcohol from two glasses daily [ADA_older_adults_2026]

avoided_actions.rationale: A gradual two-year dysexecutive decline without fluctuation or episodes; EEG would not change the diagnosis.
No parkinsonian features, no fluctuation, hallucinations or dream enactment: a dopamine transporter study has no question to answer.
No fluctuation, hallucinations or dream enactment: cardiac sympathetic imaging is a Lewy-body test with no question to answer here.
A gradual two-year decline on a background of hypertension, diabetes and a lacunar stroke gives no indication for an untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune encephalitis battery.
MRI is available and not contraindicated; CT cannot show microbleeds, siderosis or small lacunes.
A previous lacunar stroke and a purely small-vessel lesion pattern: there is no embolic pattern for an echocardiogram to explain.
Regular pulse, a lacunar stroke four years ago and no infarct of embolic shape: prolonged rhythm monitoring has no question to answer.

accepted: Vascular dementia: subcortical ischaemic (small-vessel) type with a severe dysexecutive syndrome, concealed by a normal screening score in a high-baseline patient
major neurocognitive disorder due to vascular disease

differential.key_features: The screening score and the patient's own account support it, and it is what the referral concluded, but occupational and household function are lost (FAQ 23/30) and formal executive testing is at the 1st percentile against a premorbid IQ of 128

differential.diagnosis: Occupational burnout or stress-related cognitive complaint
differential.key_features: The Geriatric Depression Scale is 3/15, the deficits are objective on formal testing, and there is a Fazekas 3 imaging burden with five lacunes
Recall is cue-responsive, recognition memory is above average, and the hippocampi are normal for age
Reduced insight is present, but there is no disinhibition, no loss of empathy, no compulsivity, no dietary change and no frontotemporal atrophy; the frontal syndrome here is subcortical and vascular
Not reported, no snoring or daytime somnolence volunteered, and the profile is not attentional

key_clinical_evidence: The threshold between mild and major cognitive disorder is functional: independence lost, not a score crossed, and a screening instrument that misses this in a highly educated patient is a ceiling artefact rather than a negative result
Premorbid ability is the reference point — a MoCA of 26 with a premorbid IQ of 128 conceals a fall of more than three standard deviations on executive measures
Ecologically valid tests are the answer to a ceiling effect: the Multiple Errands Test and a planning task detected what the bedside screen could not
Dual-task gait testing gives an objective, quantitative marker of the same executive failure and does not depend on education
The risks in this case are external as well as personal: fiduciary professional responsibility and driving both require action that a normal screen had deferred

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Emanuele Costa is a 63-year-old senior tax consultant referred after his general practitioner recorded a MoCA of 26/30 and reassured him. His wife and his business partner disagree with that reassurance, and the partner has written a letter. Over two years he has become unable to carry a case: he cannot hold the structure of a filing in mind, has missed three statutory deadlines with financial consequences, produced two returns with errors a trainee would not make, and now has a colleague covering all of his work while he remains nominally employed. At home he can no longer plan a journey with a connection, has stopped doing the family accounts, and has twice put diesel in a petrol car. His wife reports two near-misses at junctions. He himself minimises all of it and attributes the errors to a heavy workload. His memory for events is good and improves with prompting. He had a lacunar stroke four years ago with full recovery, and has hypertension, diabetes and hyperlipidaemia, all imperfectly controlled with a blood pressure of 148/88 today. There are no hallucinations, no fluctuation, no dream enactment and no gait complaint.
